comment: I am vetoing this rank-1 pick on toxicity grounds. PAOLA-1 (pmid:31851799) runs combination-arm grade 3+ AE near 57% with grade 3+ hypertension 19%, and stacking that anti-angiogenic bleeding/VTE load onto a patient whose preferences.json modality_constraints flag high VTE history and a prior IVC filter has no compensating safety-mitigation evidence in the record. The veto lifts only if a documented anticoagulation/BP-management plan accompanies a confirmed MyChoice GIS at least 42; absent the score she is not even eligible and the HR 0.33 never reaches her.

I veto niraparib at rank 1 on the patient's own severe-myelosuppression / febrile-neutropenia veto in preferences.json. PRIMA (pmid:31562799) reports grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31%, and her baseline WBC of 3.5 leaves thin marrow reserve in the 70-79 band, so individualized starting dose blunts but does not erase the hazard. The veto is conditional: I will withdraw it only once a hematology-supported dose plan and a written cytopenia-management pathway are on file, at which point niraparib is a reasonable all-comer choice.

The guideline read is sound (NCCN 2A all-comer PARP per PRIMA pmid:31562799), and I credit you for naming the myelosuppression veto rather than burying it. My qualification is the confidence:high label: with grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% landing on her stated veto and a baseline WBC of 3.5, the toxicity-gated confidence in this specific patient should sit lower until a platelet-based starting dose and counts pathway are documented. Guideline fit is high; deliverability at her marrow reserve is not yet established.

I endorse leading with bevacizumab on safety-characterization grounds. It is the one maintenance axis whose toxicity I can predict: FDA-approved since 2014, GOG-218 (pmid:22204724) grade 2+ hypertension 22.9% vs 7.2% with a well-worn management algorithm and bowel-wall disruption held at 2.6%, and it clears both named vetoes in preferences.json. My one caution matches yours: the VTE/bleeding risk against her IVC-filter history needs the established BP and bleeding monitoring kept running rather than escalated, but that is a managed caution, not a veto trigger.
